History:
- Presenting complaint: 40-year-old female with 3 weeks of left-sided hearing loss and numbness of the left face (around the jawline), accompanied by occasional tinnitus and intermittent dizziness.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began about 3 weeks ago; hearing loss and facial numbness persistent; numbness ongoing at time of consultation; no other neuro symptoms reported (no weakness, dysphagia, dysarthria, or vision changes).
- Context/triggers: Symptoms occurring on the left side; may impact work as a jockey due to dizziness and hearing issues.
- Associated symptoms: Ringing in the ear; no fever, no ear discharge, no ear pain.
- Relevant negatives: No swallowing or speech difficulty; no vision changes reported.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps (past history).
- Prior labyrinthitis (history mentioned).
- Medications: Nose spray (PRN; name unknown; prescription previously). Rennies PRN.
- Allergies: Latex.
- Family history: Brother with Neurofibromatosis.
- Social: Jockey; lives with partner; currently working with some training limitations due to symptoms.

Physical Examination:
- No formal physical examination documented (telemedicine visit); plan for in-person assessment.
- Patient-reported findings to be evaluated: Left-sided hearing loss; numbness of left face (around jawline); left ear tinnitus; occasional dizziness.
- Other negatives reported: No fever; no ear discharge; no ear pain; no dysphagia; no dysarthria; no vision changes.

Impression:
- Probable Bell's palsy or other unilateral facial neuropathy/dysfunction pending clinical confirmation; not deemed immediately life-threatening based on tele-visit assessment.

Management Plan:
- Arrange in-person, face-to-face neurological and ENT/ear examination today in a clinic in Central London.
- Objective: Neurological examination and ear examination to confirm diagnosis and assess for Bell's palsy or other etiologies.
- Reassurance given; emphasize need for physical exam to definitively reassure patient.
- Booking: Admin team to schedule same-day appointment; patient to contact support to confirm slot.
- No new medications prescribed at this time; follow-up planned based on exam results.
- Safety: Advise patient to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen or if new red flags develop.

Patient Summary:
- A 40-year-old jockey with a 3-week history of unilateral left hearing loss and facial numbness, with tinnitus and dizziness. Past history includes nasal polyps and prior labyrinthitis; latex allergy. She has been advised to undergo an in-person neurological/ENT exam today to evaluate for Bell's palsy and to obtain definitive reassurance.

Key Takeaways:
- An in-person neurological and ear examination today is essential to confirm the diagnosis.
- The clinician reassures that the condition is not immediately life-threatening but requires exam to rule out other causes.
- Schedule and complete the clinic visit today; contact support to secure a convenient appointment time in Central London.

Next Steps:
- Complete in-person neurological and ENT examination today; assess for Bell's palsy or alternative etiologies.
- Based on exam findings, develop definitive management plan (treatment, further tests, or referral as indicated).

  - Vitals (not recorded).

  - Imaging or laboratory tests discussed (none planned).
  - Definitive past medical history details beyond polyps and labyrinthitis (e.g., other chronic conditions).
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
